findings.problem: No retrieval date anywhere. Decision 10 requires every credit to carry the original date AND the date the text was truly retrieved, and the approved audit answers (decision 18: audit Q2 and Q3) set the form: written / this version / copied, with a read date only where the repository proves it. The spec's works schema (1.2), index (1.3), panel header and source line (1.6 items 2, 3, 8), shelf cards (3.5), sources.json entries and NOTICE paragraphs carry only `when` (the original date). Nothing records when each pinned copy was made, although the dates exist: the Let's Church pin 71f6f0f is committed 2026-10-09; JFB SwordVersionDate 2021-02-15, KD 2022-08-03, Barnes 2002-01-01, MHC 2022-08-29; GITenberg commits 2018-10-06 to 2018-10-21; and the Catena source records carry their own `"retrieved": "2026-07-10"` (ecatholic2000.com). The three live works are also repacked with no dates. The spec also records a `checked` scan for each `lines` row but never shows it, so a reader cannot follow a credit to a page to check it (decision 11).
findings.fix: Add to config/voices/<id>.json and the index a required `dates` object: `written` (original publication, per `lines` row where volumes differ), `version` (the upstream module or commit date), `copied` (the date the sources.json pin or mirror commit was made, from git, never typed by hand), and for the Catena the source's own `retrieved`. Show them on the book line ('written 1871; this copy: CrossWire JFB 3.0 of 15 February 2021; copied 2026-10-2x') and on each shelf card; show each `lines.checked` scan as a link ('See the printed volume'). Add a works.rs check that every work and every `lines` row has all three dates, and a verify check that the index carries them. Apply to catena-aurea, henry-concise and wesley-notes in V1, not only new works.

findings.problem: Keil and Delitzsch: the provenance and license the spec states are not what the sources say, and the mirror would redistribute CC BY-SA text with no license notice. (1) The Wikisource page the module names (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Biblical_commentary_the_Old_Testament, fetched today) says 'The source document of this text is not known', sits in 'Texts without a source', and credits 'Franz Delitzsch (1885–1892)' for all six volumes; the spec calls it 'Wikisource's transcription of T. and T. Clark's English edition (1864–78)'. (2) kd.conf says 'This module is based on the BibleWorks 8 user-created module by Willem Swanepoel, available here: http://bibleworks.oldinthenew.org/?page_id=151' (domain no longer resolves; the 2020 archived page states no license), and the spec's own '„Y' BibleWorks font codes show that text is still in it; the spec's credit omits this link of the chain. (3) Version 2.0 is dated 2022-08-03, when Wikisource text was CC BY-SA 3.0, not 4.0 (the footer moved to 4.0 in June 2023); the spec labels the source 'CC BY-SA 4.0'. (4) Section 7's SOURCE.md for mirror/sword-KD writes only 'DistributionLicense=Public Domain' and the TextSource line: a verbatim public copy of CC BY-SA text with no license, no URI and no attribution breaks the license's notice terms. (5) The `lines` plan ('checked against its title page') cannot prove which printing an unsourced text follows.
findings.fix: In 5.3: name the full chain in sources.json attribution, NOTICE.md and the panel source line (Willem Swanepoel's BibleWorks 8 module, then Wikisource, page revision and 'source document not known', then CrossWire KD 2.0 of 2022-08-03). State the source license as CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported as of that date, and ship the built files under CC BY-SA 4.0 only as an adaptation under 3.0 section 4(b), saying so; if the founder wants only a plain 4.0 source, ask him first. For KD, make the mirror workflow write into SOURCE.md the CC BY-SA 3.0 notice and URI, 'text from Wikisource contributors' with the page URL, and the CrossWire chain, before any push. Make V8 collate a sample of each volume against dated archive.org scans (the conf links biblicalcomm01keiluoft) and record which printing matches in `checked`; a volume that matches none is left out or labelled 'printing not identified'. Never reuse Wikisource's 'Franz Delitzsch (1885–1892)' author line.

findings.problem: The format plans selections that open to none of the writer's words, against decision 12 ('nothing a reader clicks may open empty'). Section 6 keeps the Matthew 23:13 Catena item 'with only the left-out lines', and 8.4 makes opening it a browser check, so a reader taps 'the Church Fathers' and sees only three 'left out' lines. Section 2.4 puts book and note left-out lines 'under that writer's place in the list of writers on the verse (shown even when that writer has no other notes on the verse)', so on 1 Timothy 1:1 a Calvin header (a button with aria-expanded, 1.6 item 2) opens to nothing but the line. The `has` rule ('set only for verses that a shown note covers') and verify item 3 do not say whether an all-left-out item counts, so the extras line may also name the Fathers there. Separately, Calvin tail-cut rule (a) cuts at the earliest ref-only paragraph, and Philemon 1:1's body (the only NT entry like this, measured in calvin.json) starts with one, so that note becomes empty.
findings.fix: Define `has` as: verses where the work has at least one shown (Said) voice. Render every left-out line (Catena all-hidden items, book and note scope) as plain, non-interactive text in a 'Left out here' list under the lead, never as a writer header, never in the extras line. Add verify checks: every set bit has a Said voice on that verse; no work section without a Said voice; no empty text. Apply the Calvin tail cut only after the first comment paragraph, and drop, with a count, any note left empty. Change the 8.4 Matthew 23:13 check to 'the Fathers are not listed; the quiet left-out line shows'. Coordinate with the no-empty-selections branch (run wf_e5046b06-4ad).

findings.problem: App-written statements about people and history carry no source, against decisions 11, 15 and 17 ('cite everything', 'every note must read as what its named sources say', 'it goes for everything'). Unsourced in the spec: every `who` note (Eusebius 'sided with Arius before the Council of Nicaea, then signed its creed'; 'Victor of Antioch, a priest of the 400s'; Gloss 'notes written in the margins'), every `reasons` line ('The Church later condemned some of his teaching'; Didymus 'Later councils condemned him with Origen'; 'Its writer is now held to have followed Arius'), the panel's 'Their words' and 'Left out' lines, shelf `what` claims (JFB's three churches; Barnes 'a Presbyterian pastor'), and the new `luther` cite entry's `why`. The one check planned (Eusebius against Socrates 1.8) proves only the signing: Eusebius's letter there does not show he sided with Arius before Nicaea (that rests on Arius's letter to Eusebius of Nicomedia, preserved by Theodoret, Church History book 1).
findings.fix: Add a required `src` to every `who`, `reasons` and app-written fact in config/voices (author, work, original date, page or URL, retrieved date), shown as a one-tap link beside the line, and refuse the build on a missing `src`. Use public-domain believing works (for example Percival, The Seven Ecumenical Councils, NPNF II vol. 14, 1900, for the 553 and later condemnations; Socrates 1.8 and Theodoret book 1 in NPNF II vols. 2 and 3 for Eusebius; Smith and Wace's Dictionary of Christian Biography, 1877–87, for the persons), or quote them. Where no source can be found, drop the claim. Shelf `what` facts get the same `src` or are reduced to what the title page itself says.

findings.problem: The Scripture-respect list is incomplete for Calvin, and the review scan would not find the gaps. Section 2.6 says 'No exclusion is known in ... Calvin's 21 books', but calvin.json at the pin has Calvin on Matthew 27:9 ('the name of Jeremiah has been put down by mistake, instead of Zechariah') and on Acts 7:16 ('it is manifest that there is a fault [mistake] in the word Abraham ... Wherefore this place must be amended'), both saying words the BSB prints are wrong; and Acts 7:14 ('this difference came through the error of the writers'). The 2.5 'error' pattern needs one of evangelist|apostle|Moses|scripture|text|writer|historian|narrative|account within 60 characters: Matthew 27:9 and Acts 7:16 have none, and 'fault', 'crept in' and 'amended' are not patterns, so both pass unflagged. The scan's 'deutero' also matches every 'Deuteronomy' (31 distinct KD entries in Deuteronomy alone), and 'Maccab' gives 68 Psalms hits in KD that mostly rebut critics, so real cases are buried.
findings.fix: List Matthew 27:9, Acts 7:14 and Acts 7:16 (Calvin) and Matthew 27:9 (Barnes: 'a mistake made by ancient transcribers ... Probably this is the correct explanation') in docs/voices/review/calvin-commentaries.md and in section 9 question 1 as a named class: 'claims that the received text (as the BSB prints it) contains a copyist's error'. Add a proposed default for that class and for textual judgements that agree with the BSB's own omissions (Barnes on Acts 8:37 'unless it is spurious', JFB and Barnes on 1 John 5:7). Extend the scan: add 'fault', 'crept in', 'amend', 'by mistake', 'corrupt', and anchors 'passage|place|name|word|copy|copies|transcrib'; make 'deutero' 'deutero-?(isaiah|zechariah|nom)' and exclude 'Deuteronomy'.

findings.problem: Section 9 question 1 misstates the Keil and Delitzsch case the founder is asked to rule on, and the real cases are missing. The spec says 'Delitzsch dates Psalm 44 ... to the Maccabees'; in the KD module Delitzsch weighs that view and rejects it ('Nevertheless many considerations are opposed to the composition of the Psalm in the time of the Maccabees'). Cases that do fit the spec's proposed default (an author named in a title) are absent: Psalm 74 ('A Maskil of Asaph'), whose shown verse comments at 74:4 ('a weighty instance in favour of the Maccabaean origin of the Psalm') and 74:18 favour a Maccabean date; Psalm 86 ('A prayer of David'), whose entry says it 'can only be called a Psalm by David as having grown out of Davidic and other model passages', repeated at Psalm 130:1 ('Ps 86 is not Davidic'); and Proverbs 1:7 to 9:18, which Delitzsch's introduction gives to 'an altogether different author from Solomon, and one who is more recent' (cut today only because introductions are cut, while Ecclesiastes for the same kind of claim is left out by book).
findings.fix: Rewrite question 1 with these quotations and their verse entries (KD Psalms 74:4, 74:18, 86:1, 130:1; Proverbs 1:1-7 introduction). Put each in docs/voices/review/keil-delitzsch.md as a proposed exclusion or 'kept' with the reason. Say explicitly that the Proverbs case is hidden only by the introduction cut, so a later change to that cut must re-check it.

findings.problem: The `expect` field has two meanings and either one breaks a first entry. 2.1 says for book scope it is 'how many source entries are removed'; 2.2 says 'The match count must equal expect, or the build fails'. Measured in calvin.json: 'THE FIRST EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY', 'SECOND EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY' and the Titus 1:1-4 ref each occur once, while their entries give expect 6, 4 and 3 (the chapter entries). Under 2.2 all three Calvin entries fail; under 2.1, `kd-ecclesiastes` (no expect, default 1) fails because KD has many Ecclesiastes entries.
findings.fix: Split the field: `matches` (how many times `words` occur where the entry says, default 1) and `removes` (required for book and note scope: how many source entries go). Set calvin-1-timothy matches 1 removes 6, calvin-2-timothy 1 and 4, calvin-titus 1 and 3, and kd-ecclesiastes matches 1 with `removes` measured by V8. Add a V1 test for each.

findings.problem: The Catena clean-up hides quotations under a reason that is false for them. Section 6 hides all 439 'Pseudo-Chrysostom' quotations in Matthew with the line 'from an unfinished work on Matthew ... Its writer is now held to have followed Arius', and NOTICE says '440 quotations from an unfinished work on Matthew'. The unfinished work has no homilies on Matthew 26 to 28 (the per-chapter counts in the pinned matthew.jsonl match its gaps: none in 9 or 14 to 18), yet 4 quotations sit in Matthew 27 and 28, three tagged as other sermons: 'Pseudo Chrys. in Hom. de Cruce et Latr.' and 'Hom. vi. in Pass.' (27:45-50) and 'Hom. de Resur. iii.' (28:1-7). The approved rule targets 'the Arian writer', not every use of the name in Matthew.
findings.fix: Hide only the unfinished work's quotations: the untagged ones in chapters it covers, plus tags naming its homilies. Show the quotations from other sermons (the 27:39-44 untagged one, the three tagged ones, and any other tag V2 cannot tie to the unfinished work) with the Luke note 'a writer once thought to be Chrysostom', as Luke's 11 are. Recount `expect`, the verify numbers and the NOTICE sentence from the data, and list the reassigned quotations in the PR for the founder.

findings.problem: The three live works are repacked with their old credits ('behaviour unchanged'), against decision 10 and the approved audit answers (decision 18: Q4 and Q16). CrossWire's mhcc.conf says the Concise 'matches the printed edition as published by Moody Press, 28th printing': it is a later abridgment, yet the panel credits 'Matthew Henry' for all 66 books with no abridger and no edition date, and from Romans on it abridges the continuators' work. Wesley's notes are credited to Wesley alone, though by his own prefaces they draw on Bengel (New Testament) and largely abridge Henry and Poole (Old Testament). The Catena line names no translators beyond 'translated 1841–45' and not the ecatholic2000.com transcription.
findings.fix: In V1, give catena-aurea, henry-concise and wesley-notes `lines` and `copy` that meet decision 10: Concise 'a later abridgment of Matthew Henry's commentary by an editor this copy does not name, as printed by Moody Press (28th printing)', with Romans to Revelation marked as abridged from the continuators; Wesley 'drawing on Bengel, Henry and Poole, as his prefaces say' (quote the prefaces, checked on a scan); Catena 'Oxford translation edited by John Henry Newman, 1841–45, transcribed by ecatholic2000.com (retrieved 2026-07-10), as kept in AlvaroBalbin/catena'. Change the acceptance in 5.0 to 'same notes, corrected credits'.

findings.problem: Henry's complete commentary credits 17 books to 'other ministers' instead of the people who wrote them (decision 10). Henry died in 1714 having reached Acts. mhc.json names a writer only for Romans (John Evans), Titus and Philemon (Jeremiah Smith), 2 and 3 John (John Reynolds) and Jude (John Billingsley), so 1 and 2 Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, 1 and 2 Thessalonians, 1 and 2 Timothy, Hebrews, James, 1 and 2 Peter, 1 John and Revelation would show no writer. The `henry` cite entry, the shelf `by` and the spec's `when` ('1706–21') against its own citation ('London, 1708–1710; completed 1721') also disagree. The file's chain is also incomplete: MHC's conf says the text came from CCEL, which got it from Logos Research.
findings.fix: Make V10 find the printed list of the ministers who finished the work (in a dated scan of the 1721 volume 6 or a 19th-century edition that prints the list) and add a `lines` row per book naming each one, with `checked` set to the scan page; if no scan names a book's writer, use the approved Q4 wording ('a minister this edition does not name'), never Henry. Correct the volume dates from the scans (volume 4 is 1712, not within 1708–1710). Credit the chain: Logos Research, CCEL, CrossWire MHC 2.2 (2022-08-29), Let's Church.

findings.problem: Calvin, JFB and Henry's complete commentary are CCEL transcriptions, and the spec never quotes or reconciles CCEL's own terms. CCEL's copyright page (saved in the research, research/ccel/ccel_copyright.html) says 'These books may be used for personal, educational, or non-profit purposes. Contact us for permission to republish CCEL works or to use them commercially.' The research rejects CCEL copies for exactly this reason elsewhere (group-luther.md: CCEL '**No**'; group-fathers.md: 'No, under the rule that the transcription itself must be free to copy'; group-reformers.md), but for these three works it takes CCEL's text through CrossWire ('take it from CrossWire, as Henry's Concise was') and the spec's license check reads only CrossWire's 'DistributionLicense=Public Domain'. CLAUDE.md requires the license 'confirmed on the source's own page'.
findings.fix: In each of 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5, quote both CCEL statements in the sources.json `license` field and NOTICE: the book-level 'Rights: Public Domain' (VOICES-PLAN says jfb.txt opens with it; check calcom and mhc the same way) and the site policy above. Ask the founder for one recorded rule (CCEL's per-book public-domain mark suffices, as already accepted for Henry Concise, Easton and Smith, or it does not) and apply it the same way to Luther, Edwards and the fathers, which the research rejected. Until he rules, keep these three works out of PR order.

findings.problem: JFB's words are not as printed, and the credit hides why. The research (group-1.md section 5) collated the module against the 1873 printing: the e-text writes 'namely' for 'viz.', 'further' for 'farther' and 'favor' for 'favour', and abbreviates references; the text that travels with it says 'This expanded edition ... prepared from text scanned by Woodside Bible Fellowship'. The spec's NOTICE paragraph names only the reference abbreviations and says 'copied word for word', and the attribution skips Woodside Bible Fellowship and CCEL's role.
findings.fix: State in `copy`, NOTICE.md and the panel source line that this is an electronic 'expanded edition' (Woodside Bible Fellowship's scan, by way of CCEL's jfb.txt, then CrossWire JFB 3.0) that modernizes some words and spellings ('namely' for 'viz.'), with the measured examples. Keep 'word for word from this copy', never 'as printed'. Have V7 record a short collation per author against the archive.org scan (commentarycritic00jami) in docs/voices/review/jfb.md.

findings.problem: Barnes would ship with no named edition, no original date for the words shown and no known source. barnes.conf has no TextSource and only 'DistributionLicense=Public Domain' (SwordVersionDate 2002-01-01); the spec itself says its John 3:16 note 'follows a later printing than that of 1858'. Decision 10 needs the edition read from and the original date, and the true writer: a later printing may carry an editor's revisions (for example a 19th-century edited reissue), which would then be shown as Barnes's words.
findings.fix: Make V11 collate 3 to 5 notes against dated scans of the main printings (the first volumes of the 1830s, the 1850s revised printings, the 1868–72 Harper printing and the 1884–85 edited reissue), name the printing that matches in `lines` with `checked`, and name any editor whose words it carries. If none matches, ship with the line 'from a printing after 1858 that this copy does not name' on screen (not only in NOTICE), or hold Barnes for the founder.

findings.problem: The spec makes CLAUDE.md and docs/HANDOFF.md binding without saying that decisions 13 and 15 replace their 'Disclose AI drafting' rule ('Every AI-drafted passage and card says "Drafted with AI help (Claude) ..."'). V12 edits Layers passages in Ecclesiastes, where the live UI carries that line; a module that follows CLAUDE.md as told would add or keep AI wording on notes and sources, which the founder has now forbidden anywhere ('No crediting of AI').
findings.fix: Add to 'Binding inputs': 'Decisions 13 and 15 replace the CLAUDE.md and HANDOFF rule "Disclose AI drafting": no AI wording on any note, summary, source or credit.' Add to V12's acceptance that its passages carry no AI line and that each edited note reads as what its named sources say, with their words one tap away. Note that the CLAUDE.md and HANDOFF update decision 13 asks for belongs in PR-2 (or a separate PR that lands first).

findings.problem: The reader line for `kd-ecclesiastes` credits the wrong writers: 'Keil and Delitzsch's notes on Ecclesiastes are left out, because they deny that Solomon wrote it.' The Ecclesiastes commentary is Franz Delitzsch's alone (the spec's own `why` says so). The words themselves are confirmed: they are in the KD module's Ecclesiastes 1:1 entry (146,750 characters, introduction in a verse slot), so `found` is right.
findings.fix: Line: 'Franz Delitzsch's notes on Ecclesiastes (in Keil and Delitzsch's commentary) are left out, because he holds that Solomon did not write the book.'

findings.problem: Two panel lines promise what the build does not deliver. 'Their words are shown as printed' is false for Calvin (CCEL's American spelling), JFB (modernized e-text), Graebner's Galatians (abridged, 'put into modern English') and KD (unsourced Wikisource text). 'Any passage in any writer that denies Scripture is left out' cannot be guaranteed: the scan misses cases (see the Calvin finding) and proposed entries wait for the founder.
findings.fix: 'Their words are shown as each copy named below has them.' and 'Passages found to deny Scripture are left out, and the place is marked; so are quotations from writers the early Church condemned.' Give each line a source per decision 11.

findings.problem: KD's garbled BibleWorks font code is handled two incompatible ways. Reader step 3 says a paragraph with '„Y' runs and no scan proof 'stays as it is and is named in NOTICE.md'; verify says 'no shown KD text contains ... "„Y" (unless named in fixes)', which fails the build on that same paragraph. Showing font-code junk also misrepresents the print.
findings.fix: Replace each unproven run with the reserved mark {"k": "gap", "t": "[Hebrew word not legible in this copy]"} and count them; keep verify's ban on raw '„Y'; list the places in NOTICE.md.

findings.problem: The record of who decided what cannot be re-checked by anyone else. Every `decided` value cites 'FOUNDER-DECISIONS-2026-10-20.md', a file in the founder's work folder, not the repository (decision 11: 'The attribution evidence is kept in the repository'). The spec also cites 'decision 12' for the avoid-list rule and 'decision 13' for many writers on a verse; in that file decision 12 is 'Nothing that opens empty' and decision 13 is about AI summaries (the rules meant are shortlist questions 12 and 13).
findings.fix: Commit the founder's decisions as docs/decisions.md in PR-2 (the HANDOFF already proposes it) and point every `decided` there, by heading. Change the spec's references to 'shortlist question 12' and 'shortlist question 13' (and 'shortlist question 11' for flate2).

findings.problem: The Calvin incomplete-copy line understates what is cut: 'this copy keeps only a few lines of each chapter'. Measured: the 13 Pastoral entries keep 394 to 1,586 words each (9,533 in all), the comment on each chapter's opening verses.
findings.fix: 'Calvin's notes on 1 Timothy are left out: this copy keeps only the start of each chapter's comments (about 9,500 of Calvin's words on these letters).' Give the 197,000 figure a source or drop it.

findings.problem: Luther credits are not quite true to the books. Genesis volume 1's title page reads 'Based on Dr. Henry Cole's translation from the original Latin. Revised, enlarged, parts retranslated and edited in complete form by John Nicholas Lenker' (Lutherans in All Lands Co., Minneapolis, 1904), not 'translated by Lenker from Cole's version'. The Genesis lectures were prepared for print by Veit Dietrich and others, and the 1535 Galatians from Georg Rörer's notes. The shelf claim 'the book of his own he loved best' rests on one remark in Graebner's preface ('There is one book that Luther himself likes better than any other'), while Luther's 1537 letter to Capito named only The Bondage of the Will and the Catechism.
findings.fix: Line: 'Henry Cole's translation, revised, enlarged and partly retranslated by John Nicholas Lenker (Minneapolis, 1904)'. Add to `how` or the line 'lectures prepared for print by his students (Veit Dietrich and others)' and, for Galatians, 'from Georg Rörer's notes', each with a source. Drop 'loved best', or quote it as the preface's words, credited to Graebner.

findings.problem: The Galatians copy is an old snapshot, and its first source goes uncredited. The GITenberg commit e362c0a is from 2018-10-21; Project Gutenberg's own page now shows 'Most recently updated: February 17, 2024'. Word-diffing the two (ignoring quote styles) leaves only 'VERSE 6.' corrected to 'VERSE 5.' and 'Jews' to 'Jews.', which the spec patches by hand as GALATIANS_FIXES. The text's own closing note, which the reader strips and verify forbids, says it 'was converted to ASCII format for Project Wittenberg by Laura J. Hoelter and is in the public domain. You may freely distribute, copy or print this text.' That is the first source's own license words, and nothing credits it.
findings.fix: Either mirror the current Project Gutenberg file (mirror-web-texts.yml, mirror/pg-1549) and drop the fix, or keep GITenberg and say in the credit 'Project Gutenberg ebook 1549 as copied by GITenberg in October 2018'. Either way, name Project Wittenberg (Concordia Theological Seminary) and Laura J. Hoelter in the chain, and quote its public-domain sentence in sources.json `license`.

findings.problem: Two Catena voices are kept without a recorded decision. Clement of Alexandria, whom the approved fathers list puts under 'Leave out the disputed for now', keeps his one Luke quotation (with only the spelling fix). Josephus keeps his one Matthew quotation as a voice under 'the Church Fathers' in 'Christian writers', while CLAUDE.md says Josephus may be named 'only as witnesses, never as a citation'.
findings.fix: Give Clement a `who` row with a source, as the approved answer did for Eusebius, and list him in the PR for the founder. Give Josephus the note 'the Jewish historian of the first century, quoted by Aquinas as a witness; not a Christian writer', with a source, or hide him with a truthful reason if the founder prefers.

findings.problem: FOUNDER-DECISIONS-2026-10-20.md still lists the Luther plan's question 14 ('Graebner's abridged Galatians') as 'Still open', while the spec ships it in PR-7 on the strength of the shortlist's approved question 3. Decision 4 also asks that words left out of an original be 'shown honestly'; Graebner's abridgment leaves words out with no marks, and only the book line says 'abridged'.
findings.fix: Add it to section 9 as a confirmation: 'Graebner's Galatians ships labelled "abridged, put into modern English by Theodore Graebner"; it has no marks where Luther's words are left out. Confirm, or wait for a full text.'

revise.summary:
I rewrote VOICES-BUILD-SPEC.md (about 1,190 lines, no em dashes). It closes every blocker and major from the three reviews: feasibility 20, reader 17 and rules 23. Most minors are closed too. Section 10 is the review record: one row per finding, saying where it is closed. Nothing in the repository was changed; I used git fetch, git show, read-only gh api calls and the research copies already on disk.

**Current state.** origin/main is now 2aabdcc (PR #50, the Layers mend, merged). The commentary notice exists only as the unpushed local commit d12a4dd on commentary-notice. The true-credits branch has no commits of its own. No no-empty-selections branch exists yet.

**What changed in the spec:**

1. **Dates (decision 10, audit questions 2 and 3).** Every work now carries three dates: written, this version and copied, plus retrieved where the source records one. Measured values:
   - The Let's Church files are dated 2026-06-30 (bb79df2); the pin commit 71f6f0f is 2026-10-09; the app pinned it on 2026-10-10 (38749bd).
   - The CrossWire module dates come from the confs: JFB 2021-02-15, KD 2022-08-03, MHC 2022-08-29, MHCC 2021-02-14, Calvin 2022-08-01, Wesley 2001-11-28 and Barnes 2002-01-01.
   - The Catena's own records say ecatholic2000.com was read on 2026-07-10. That is later than its file's 2026-05-02 commit; the spec says so.
   - The dates show on the book line and the shelf cards. scripts/voices-dates.mjs checks copied against git, so the value is typed once and still checked.
2. **Every person or history claim needs a source.** People notes, `who` notes and reasons each carry a source (writer, work, date, page, URL, read date, quote), kept in docs/evidence files. The build refuses one without it. A claim with no source is dropped.
3. **Nothing opens empty (decision 12).**
   - A writer is listed only where it has words on that verse.
   - Pointer-only and empty notes are dropped. That aligns with the no-empty-selections findings (Wesley 139, Henry Concise on Isaiah 36).
   - Matthew 23:13, where every Fathers quotation is hidden, becomes a plain "Left out here" line, as do the book-scope lines.
   - Calvin's tail cut now applies only after the first comment paragraph, which fixes Philemon 1:1.
4. **The panel follows the notice commit d12a4dd.** It uses `commentary: true` and `closed()`. There is no own opt-in and no Hide button. The remembered-writers migration runs when the module loads, so it works even after the notice deletes the old key.
5. **Long notes are cut per quotation, not per passage,** and only for works that set a length. The three live works have no long files. Openings now end at a real sentence end, not after a numeral or list marker.
6. **Exclusions:**
   - Each work's exclusions live in its own config file.
   - The old `expect` field is split into `matches` and `removes`. The Calvin words were each measured as appearing once.
   - New proposed class: passages saying the BSB's words are a copyist's mistake (Calvin on Matthew 27:9, Acts 7:14 and 7:16; Barnes on Matthew 27:9).
